text:
maya: rolling up a new int8 reranker 'rangr-3b-int8' to staging  smoke eval looks off, ndcg@10 ~ -3.4% rel, mrr ~ -2.1%. tagging eng-ml for triage. anyone free?
onkar: what's the exact eval command / dataset? ndcg@10 or @5? :thinking:
sarah: ndcg@10 and MRR. eval run on holdout_seed42 (prod-like). maya, can you paste the command you used?
maya: sure  `./eval.sh --model rangr-3b-int8 --holdout holdout_seed42 --metrics ndcg@10,mrr --topk 100`
maya: quick paste from the run (aggregates):
```
baseline (fp16): ndcg@10=0.412, mrr=0.288
rangr-3b-int8: ndcg@10=0.398, mrr=0.282
rel drop: ndcg -3.4% (p<0.01), mrr -2.1%
```
leo: suspicious  did you use identical tokenization + priming? small token shifts can kill tail queries. check tokenizer.hash/version and prompt template.
onkar: also check batching/kvpack differences  int8 build used continuous-batching tweak and kvpack=true. that can alter candidate ordering when truncation happens.
maya: confirmed tokenizer match. tokenizer.vocab_hash=0x9a7f. Prompt template identical. kvpack was enabled for speed on staging.
sarah: can you re-run with kvpack=false as an A/B? quick smoke on 10k queries should tell.
maya: kicking off quick ab (kvpack=false) now. cmd: `./eval.sh --model rangr-3b-int8 --holdout sample_10k --kvpack false`
rerank-bot: evaluation job queued  job id 67321  staging cluster (p3x2) :eyes:
onkar: also check PTQ calibration data. was it calibrated on the same query/doc length distribution? mismatched calib sets often bias short query signal.
leo: another common failure  quant backend switch. did the int8 use per-channel weights or per-tensor? show quant config.
maya: here's the quant config we used:
```
quant.backend = xnnpack
weights.mode = per_tensor
activation.mode = asym_uint8
calib.sample_size = 51200
```
leo: try per_channel weights + symmetric activations for test, or at least per_channel for attention layers.
sarah: also run a quick slice analysis: short-queries (<=6 tokens) vs long-queries, and candidate-length buckets. share ndcg per-slice.
maya: running slice job now. will paste results in ~15m.
onkar: for reproducibility, add `--seed 42` to the eval run and pin batch size to same as baseline (bs=64). tiny batching differences change truncation order.
maya: noted. adding seed + bs.
rerank-bot: job 67322 started (slice-analysis). ETA ~12m.
sarah: if kvpack toggle fixes it we might revisit the runtime optimization (we enabled kvpack by default for int8 rollout). if not, might be quantization artifact. either way make a small canary: rollout 2% while we investigate.
leo: also upload a handful of failing query examples to the eval dashboard (link below) so we can inspect actual text/context. https://dash.internal/rerank/67322 :point_left:
maya: uploaded 25 failing queries + candidate text. early glance shows some short queries getting identical top-3 ordering swapped.
onkar: when you have the slice results pls post ndcg by bucket and the top-k changes for random seeds. if we see deterministic reorder maybe it's tokenizer/truncation, if variance high maybe quant noise.
maya: slice results (summary):
```
short_queries (<=6): ndcg@10 baseline 0.389 -> int8 0.356 (drop 8.5%)
mid_queries (7-20): ndcg drop ~1.2%
long_queries (>20): ndcg slightly up 0.3%
```
sarah: OK that screams truncation/priming or candidate window change on short queries. kvpack likely the main suspect.
leo: agree. if kvpack packs more candidates into the same token budget we might be shifting which parts of doc are visible. try with kvpack=false + per_channel quant.
maya: queued re-run with per_channel & kvpack=false, seed pinned. job 67323.
rerank-bot: job 67323 queued  will notify on completion.
onkar: good. also snapshot model ONNX export and run the eval in cpu fp16 to rule out runtime math differences.
sarah: if per_channel helps, we should update quant profiles and re-run a 100k holdout before promoting. also add a regression alert for short-query slice on next canary.
maya: thanks all  will collect results and post follow-up. leaving rollout at 0% for now. :thumbsup:
onkar: ping me when job 67323 completes, I can help dig into failing examples.
leo: if still bad after per_channel, we'll try a light L2 distill step from fp16 to int8 to recover ranking for short queries.
maya: noted. will update in this thread.
